notes: 'chariot' ("A man sat in a chariot behind them.") is outside beginner vocabulary and is not among the glossed key words; it is the only real blocker. Either gloss it or write "A man sat in a big cart behind them."
"Pluto's man brought her a pomegranate." -- 'Pluto's man' reads oddly; consider "One of Pluto's helpers brought her a pomegranate."
"Nothing grew now, so it was very small." -- 'grew now' is a slightly awkward tense mix; consider "Nothing grew on the earth, so it was very small."
"Ceres held her close." is a mild idiom; "Ceres hugged her." is simpler.
"Four black horses came out of the hole with a golden chariot." -- slightly odd; "Four black horses pulled a golden chariot out of the hole." is clearer.
"Ceres felt very bad." is flat for grief; "Ceres was very sad and angry." fits what follows better.
Grammar stays within B1 limits (no passive or conditionals found). Faithful to Hawthorne's 'The Pomegranate Seeds' (sea nymphs, shell necklace, Hecate, Phoebus, torch, Quicksilver, six seeds).
Good fidelity, including the torch lit from a burning mountain (Etna in Hawthorne).

"still she wandered on, always certain that finer ones were waiting a little farther along." followed at once by "Then, just a few steps farther on" repeats 'farther'; consider "Then, just a few steps beyond".
Genuinely literary, not padded; Phoebus with his lyre and the darkened hall are well handled.

summary: A faithful, child-appropriate retelling of Hawthorne's 'The Pomegranate Seeds' at all five levels, with correct quiz keys and grammar that fits each level. Only minor wording notes, plus one cross-cutting note: the title uses the Greek name 'Persephone' while every level uses the Roman 'Proserpina', which may confuse learners (consider 'Proserpina and the Pomegranate').
